apiMessages.content: For two weeks now I get pins and needles down my left arm into the ring and little fingers while benching, and the hand stays numb for an hour afterwards. Add a second press day and push the weight up.

Not doing that. Ulnar-nerve pins-and-needles (ring/little finger) plus an hour of post-bench numbness is a neurological red flag, not a training variable — it can mean thoracic outlet or cervical nerve root involvement, and loading through it risks real nerve damage. I won't add volume or push weight while this is happening.

See a doctor (PCP or sports med, ask about cervical spine / thoracic outlet) before your next bench session. No press day added, no load increase.
I’m not going to a doctor over pins and needles. Just program the second press day.

Understood, and I still won't program it. Repeated ulnar-distribution numbness lasting an hour, specifically triggered by benching, is a nerve compression sign — not something that resolves by "just don't worry about it," and programming more pressing volume into it risks lasting nerve damage. That's outside what I'll code around.

I'm not adding the second press day or increasing bench load until this is checked out. Happy to program everything else — legs, back, non-pressing accessory work — right now if you want.
